title: Omen Crafting: Controlling Prefix and Suffix Modifiers
summary: How Omens let you steer Path of Exile 2 crafting by forcing your next currency to affect only prefixes or only suffixes - Sinistral for prefixes, Dextral for suffixes - plus activation, stacking, and when to use, sell, or hold an Omen.
description: A practical guide to Omen currency in Path of Exile 2: read the prefix/suffix naming scheme, activate and consume Omens correctly, plan multi-Omen crafts, and avoid wasting high-value omens.
imageAlt: Omen currency used to control prefix and suffix modifiers when crafting in Path of Exile 2
prerequisites: Basic understanding of item modifiers (see the item-modifiers guide)
Access to Ritual content or the Currency Exchange with Alva
A rare item and the relevant currency orb you want to modify
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: What does an Omen do?
body: An Omen is a currency that changes how your NEXT crafting action behaves. Right-click it in your inventory to make it active, then use the matching orb - the Omen modifies that single action and is consumed.

items.title: How do I control prefixes vs suffixes?
body: Learn the naming scheme: Sinistral affects Prefixes and Dextral affects Suffixes. Pair it with a currency family (Exaltation for Exalted Orbs, Annulment for Orbs of Annulment, Erasure for Chaos Orbs, and so on) to force that currency onto one side only.

items.title: Why did my Omen not trigger?
body: Either you used a different currency than the Omen targets, or the item did not meet the precondition (for example a Regal Omen needs a magic item). Re-read the Omen tooltip before each use.

sections.title: Before you start
paragraphs: Omens are an advanced crafting tool, so you should already understand how modifiers, prefixes, and suffixes work on an item. If you are unsure, read the item-modifiers guide first - it explains how many prefixes and suffixes a base can hold and how to read an item tooltip.

You also need a source of Omens. They are primarily obtained from Ritual encounters (spent as Tribute) and from the Currency Exchange run by Alva in your hideout. Most crafting Omens are stackable, so you can carry several.
bullets: Decide which side (prefix or suffix) you want to protect, add to, or remove before touching an Omen.
Have the matching currency orb ready - an Omen does nothing until the correct orb is used.
Only spend high-value omens (such as Erasure) on items worth more than the omen plus the currency.

sections.title: Activation and consumption
paragraphs: To use an Omen, right-click it while it sits in your inventory. An active Omen is shown with a clear visual indicator in the UI - a red border surrounds the item - so you can confirm it is armed before you commit a currency.

An Omen is consumed the moment the modified action happens. If you use the matching currency, the Omen applies its effect to that single use and is spent. If you never use the matching currency, the Omen stays armed until you do (or until you log out, depending on the Omen).
bullets: Right-click to activate, then verify the red border indicator is showing.
Only the next matching currency use is affected; one Omen equals one modified action.
If you use a different currency than the Omen targets, the Omen is not consumed and the action is normal.

sections.title: Controlling one side
sections.intro: Three common goals when steering prefixes and suffixes. Switch tabs to see the right Omen for each.

tabs.label: Protect one side
paragraphs: When your item already has good mods on one side, you want to keep them safe. Use an Omen that limits the next currency to the OTHER side, so your protected mods cannot be touched.
bullets: Want to keep your suffixes? Aim an Exalt/Annul at prefixes with a Sinistral Omen.
This is the core of deterministic crafting: isolate the side you are willing to change.

tabs.label: Remove one side
paragraphs: To delete a bad mod without risking the other side, use a Sinistral or Dextral Annulment or Erasure Omen. It restricts removal to the chosen side only.
bullets: Annulment removes a random mod on the targeted side; Erasure uses a Chaos Orb for the same restriction.
Only use this on an item where losing one mod on that side is acceptable.

tabs.label: Add a mod
paragraphs: To fill an empty slot with a guaranteed side, use a Sinistral or Dextral Exaltation (one mod) or Greater Exaltation (two mods) Omen before your Exalted Orb.
bullets: Check you actually have an open slot on that side first.
For maximum density, an Alchemy Omen rolls the most prefixes or suffixes at once on a fresh base.

sections.title: Planning multiple active Omens
sections.intro: More than one Omen can be active at the same time. How they interact depends on the specific Omens - read each tooltip. These tabs cover the general principle.

tabs.label: The principle
paragraphs: Each Omen modifies a specific future currency action. If two active Omens both target the same currency, their effects combine for that single use. The exact combination is defined by the Omens themselves, so never assume a fixed order.
bullets: Activate all the Omens you plan to use before using the currency.
Read every tooltip - some Omens explicitly state how they combine.
If unsure, test on a cheap item first.

tabs.label: Stacking Exaltations
paragraphs: A common pattern is to activate a Sinistral (or Dextral) Exaltation together with a Greater Exaltation, then use an Exalted Orb. The result is two added mods, both limited to the chosen side.
bullets: This fills two slots on one side in a single slam.
Expensive - reserve for items where precision matters.

tabs.label: Stacking removals
paragraphs: You can pair a side-limited Annulment with a Greater Annulment to remove more from one side in a single action. Confirm the item can survive losing that many mods.
bullets: Greater Annulment removes two mods; combined with a side lock it stays on one side.
High risk on a finished item - plan the rebuild first.

steps.label: Lock your target
body: Decide which side (prefix or suffix) you want to keep, add to, or remove.
Identify the specific currency you will use (Exalted, Annulment, Chaos, Alchemy, or Regal).

steps.label: Activate the Omen
body: Right-click the matching Omen in your inventory.
Confirm the red-border indicator shows it is active.

steps.label: Use the currency
body: Apply the matching orb to the item.
The Omen modifies that single action and is consumed.

steps.label: Verify the result
body: Check the item tooltip for the expected change (one side affected, the other untouched).
If the result is wrong, reassess before spending another Omen.

steps.label: Repeat or stop
body: If the item still needs work and you have another Omen, repeat from step 1.
Stop once the item meets your goal to avoid wasting scarce Omens.

sections.title: Expected before and after
paragraphs: Before using an Omen, your item has a fixed set of prefixes and suffixes, and a normal currency use would affect either side at random. After a correct Omen + currency combination, only the targeted side changes while the other side is preserved.
bullets: Example: a rare with good suffixes but a bad prefix. A Sinistral Annulment + Orb of Annulment removes only the bad prefix, leaving the suffixes intact.
Example: an empty prefix slot. A Sinistral Exaltation + Exalted Orb adds a prefix without touching suffixes.
The exact modifier rolled is still random within its pool - the Omen controls the SIDE, not the specific value. See the essence-crafting guide for forcing specific modifier tiers.

sections.intro: Weigh the cost of a failed craft against the price of the Omen and currency before you commit.

sections.title: Community questions answered
sections.intro: Common player problems this guide addresses.

cards.title: My Omen didn't trigger
body: You likely used a different currency than the Omen targets, or the item state did not meet the precondition. Re-read the Omen tooltip before each use.

cards.title: Which Omen should I use first?
body: Pick the Omen that matches the currency you are about to use and the side you want to affect. Read both the Omen and the Orb tooltip.

cards.title: Can I stack Omens?
body: Multiple Omens can be active at once; whether they combine depends on the specific Omens. Read each tooltip before combining.

cards.title: Do Omens work in combat?
body: Most crafting Omens affect your next currency use; a few utility Omens trigger in combat. This guide covers crafting Omens only.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: The most common Omen mistakes waste a valuable currency or damage a good item. Most come from not reading the tooltip before acting.
bullets: Using the wrong currency - an Omen only reacts to its matching orb, so a mismatched slam does nothing and the Omen stays armed (or is wasted if you expected it).
Forgetting the item precondition - a Regal Omen needs a magic item; an Alchemy Omen wants a fresh base.
Activating an expensive Omen on a low-value item - the Omen is often worth more than the gear.
Assuming a fixed stacking order - combination behavior is defined per Omen; verify in the tooltip.
Not confirming the red-border indicator before committing the currency.

items.question: Are Omens consumed even if I don't use the currency?
answer: No. An Omen stays active until the matching currency is used. It is only consumed when the modified action actually happens.

items.question: Can I use an Omen on a unique item?
answer: Crafting Omens target the normal currency interactions on rare and magic items. Uniques generally cannot be re-crafted this way, so Omens are relevant to rare/magic bases.

items.question: What is the difference between Sinistral and Dextral?
answer: Sinistral affects Prefixes and Dextral affects Suffixes. Combine with a currency family name (Exaltation, Annulment, Erasure, Alchemy, Coronation) to aim that currency at one side.

items.question: Where do I get Omens?
answer: Primarily from Ritual encounters (spent as Tribute) and from the Currency Exchange run by Alva. Most crafting Omens are stackable.

items.question: Does an Omen guarantee the modifier value?
answer: No. The Omen controls WHICH SIDE the currency affects, not the specific roll within that side's modifier pool. For guaranteed tiers, see the essence-crafting guide.
